questions.prompt: You've just introduced yourself and the charity. The person who picked up says a flat 'yeah, go on.' You:

options.text: Launch straight into the mission and the ask, since they said to go on
Speed up slightly so you don't lose them before you get to the point
Ask if now is actually a good time before you continue
Say 'sounds like now's not great, is it a bad time?' and wait for a real answer
Thank them for staying on the line and continue at the same pace

questions.prompt: A donor says, in a clipped tone, 'I already give to a couple of charities.' You:

options.text: Explain why your cause is more urgent right now than most
Ask which charities, so you can compare your cause to theirs
Say 'you're already doing your bit then' and pause to see where they take it
Thank them for giving and move straight to a smaller, easier ask
Reflect it back: 'a couple of charities already?' and hold the silence

questions.prompt: You state the suggested monthly amount and the line goes quiet for a few seconds. You:

options.text: Fill the gap straight away with a cheaper option
Repeat the amount in case they didn't hear it clearly
Ask 'what's on your mind?' and let them answer in their own time
Stay quiet and let the silence sit until they speak first
Explain the tax-deductible receipt to make the number feel smaller

questions.prompt: Unprompted, a donor says 'my dad went through this a few years back.' You:

options.text: Say 'sorry to hear that' and move straight back to the pitch
Note it as a good sign and go for the ask while they're engaged
Ask a gentle follow-up: 'how's he doing now?'
Slow right down and let them tell you as much or as little as they want
Name it: 'that sounds like it's still close to home for you' and wait

questions.prompt: The donor sounds warm when you open, then goes flat the moment you mention cost. You:

options.text: Push on with the pitch since they were friendly a second ago
Jump to a lower amount before they can say no
Ask directly if the amount is a problem for them
Name the shift: 'you went a bit quiet there, is it the amount?'
Slow down and ask what would feel more comfortable

questions.prompt: You can hear kids in the background and the donor's answers are getting shorter. You:

options.text: Talk faster to get through the pitch before they hang up
Keep going at the same pace, it's not your problem if it's a bad moment
Ask if it's a houseful right now and offer to call back
Notice it out loud and offer a better time, no pressure either way
Wrap the pitch up quickly and ask for a decision now

questions.prompt: A donor starts venting about cost-of-living pressure, nothing to do with your call. You:

options.text: Let them finish, then redirect straight back to the ask
Say 'I hear you' quickly and move on
Ask a question that connects what they said to a smaller, easier gift
Fully listen, reflect back what you heard, then let them decide what happens next
Name what they're feeling and ask them to say more before mentioning the charity again

questions.prompt: The donor keeps saying 'yeah, sure, sure' but sounds miles away. You:

options.text: Repeat the impact stats in a different way to try to land it
Ask them straight out if they're still keen to keep talking
Ask an open question: 'what matters most to you when you think about giving?'
Name it: 'you've gone quiet on me, has something changed?'
Ease off and give them space to come back into the conversation

questions.prompt: The donor's tone turns sharp: 'How did you even get this number?' You:

options.text: Defend the call straight away by explaining your legal right to call
Apologise repeatedly and rush to end the call
Explain plainly where the number came from and why you're calling
Acknowledge the sharpness first: 'fair question, let me explain', then answer it straight
Name it: 'that's caught you off guard' and then explain calmly

questions.prompt: A donor asks, half-joking, half-serious: 'Do you actually care about this, or is it just a job?' You:

options.text: Laugh it off and steer straight back to the script
Recite the mission statement as proof that you care
Give a short, honest answer about why you took the job
Answer honestly and ask what made them ask that
Name what's under the question: 'sounds like you've been burned by a call like this before'

questions.prompt: A donor's voice catches as they explain why the cause matters to them. You:

options.text: Keep the pitch moving so it doesn't get awkward
Say 'that's so sad' and change the subject
Say 'take your time' and wait quietly
Ask a soft follow-up question about what they said
Name it gently: 'that clearly still means a lot to you' and let them lead

questions.prompt: An elderly donor is enjoying the chat and keeps drifting off-topic. You:

options.text: Cut in and steer firmly back to the ask, you're on the clock
Let the call run long and never get to the ask at all
Enjoy a minute of it, then warmly bridge back: 'I'd love to keep chatting, and I also want to tell you about...'
Name the enjoyment: 'you're easy to talk to' and steer back gently after
Politely mention you have other calls waiting

questions.prompt: A donor demands: 'How much of my money actually goes to admin and wages?' You:

options.text: Get defensive and list reasons the overhead is justified
Dodge the number and pivot straight back to the cause
Give the honest figure plainly, no spin
Give the honest figure, then ask what prompted the question
Say you don't have that figure and offer to send it later

questions.prompt: A donor snaps: 'Take me off your list, I'm on the Do Not Call Register.' You:

options.text: Explain that registered charities are exempt from that register
Try one more time for a smaller, one-off gift before you let it go
Apologise and end the call without confirming anything further
Confirm you'll remove them, ask for the best way to action it, and thank them
Confirm you'll remove them and end the call there

questions.prompt: Three hang-ups in a row this hour. The next call is about to connect. You:

options.text: Carry the last call's tone into this one and rush the opener
Take a breath, reset, and open this call exactly as if it's the first of the day
Skim through the pitch faster to get through more calls
Mentally brace for another knock-back before they've even answered
Take a short break before dialling again

questions.prompt: A donor says: 'Are you even a real charity, or is this a scam?' You:

options.text: Get defensive: 'I can assure you this is completely legitimate'
Laugh it off, it's an odd thing to ask
Give the charity's ABN or registration and offer to let them call the charity direct to confirm
Explain the charity's registration status
Say you understand the concern and explain calmly how they can verify it

questions.prompt: Mid-pitch, the donor says 'I have to go.' You:

options.text: Talk faster to squeeze the ask in before they hang up
Ask for thirty more seconds to finish the point
Let them go straight away and offer to call back another time
Let them go, thank them for their time, no strings attached
Ask if you can at least send some information by email

questions.prompt: You've just named the monthly amount. Five full seconds of silence follow. You:

options.text: Jump in with a cheaper alternative before they can say no
Repeat the amount, maybe it didn't land
Ask 'what are you thinking?' and let them answer
Hold the silence and let them be the one to speak next
Fill the gap by listing more of the charity's programs

questions.prompt: You've got about twenty seconds before most people decide whether to keep listening. You open with:

options.text: The charity's full name and how long it's been operating
A general statistic about how many Australians the cause affects
A one-line question about whether they've heard of the charity
A short, specific line about what one gift actually changes: 'twenty dollars covers a week of meals for a family like the Turners'
A broad statement about the importance of generosity in Australia

questions.prompt: A donor asks: 'What does my fifty dollars actually do?' You respond with:

options.text: A rundown of the charity's total annual budget
A general line about how every dollar helps
A concrete example: what fifty dollars specifically funds, in real terms
A short story about one person it helped, ending on what changed for them
A comparison to what fifty dollars buys elsewhere, like two coffees a week

questions.prompt: A donor says: 'I usually just give to [a bigger, more famous charity].' You:

options.text: Point out flaws in the bigger charity to make yours look better
Argue that your charity needs the money more
Ask what they like about giving to that charity
Agree that's a great cause, then tell one specific story that shows what makes this one different
List your charity's achievements compared to theirs

questions.prompt: A donor asks you to explain the mission in one line. You say:

options.text: A line straight from the website's About page
A long explanation covering every program the charity runs
One plain sentence about who it helps and how
One plain sentence, then a real example that brings it to life
The charity's official slogan

questions.prompt: You're ready to make the ask itself. You:

options.text: Ask an open-ended 'would you consider supporting us?'
List three possible amounts and ask them to pick
Suggest a specific monthly amount tied directly to the impact story you just told
Ask for the biggest amount first to leave room to negotiate down
Ask if they can give 'whatever they're comfortable with'

questions.prompt: The donor gives a soft 'maybe, send me something to look at.' You:

options.text: Push for a firm yes before you let the call end
Agree straight away and end the call there
Agree, confirm exactly what you'll send and when, and set a real follow-up time
Agree and mention you'll try calling again in a few weeks
Try a smaller, cheaper ask instead before giving up

questions.prompt: A donor goes quiet mid-sentence, like they started to say something and stopped. You:

options.text: Carry on talking to cover the awkward gap
Assume they got distracted and repeat your last point
Wait a beat, then ask 'what were you going to say?'
Name it: 'sounds like something crossed your mind there'
Move straight to the next part of the pitch

questions.prompt: Five seconds of dead air follow right after you ask for the gift. Your gut says:

options.text: Fill it immediately with reassurance about the cause
Repeat the ask in slightly different words
They're processing, so you hold the silence
Ask if they have any questions before deciding
Summarise the impact points again in case they forgot

questions.prompt: The donor's tone shifts from friendly to clipped partway through the call. Your gut says:

options.text: They're just busy, keep the pitch moving at the same pace
Something changed, so you slow down and check in before continuing
They've decided no already, so you rush to wrap up
Push through to the ask before it gets worse
Soften your tone and ask if it's still an alright time

questions.prompt: You get voicemail instead of a person. Your instinct is to:

options.text: Leave the full pitch, amount and all, in case they don't call back
Hang up without a message and try again straight away
Leave a short, warm message with a reason to call back, and note it for a later attempt
Leave a message reading from the script word for word
Text the number immediately after, uninvited

questions.prompt: A donor says 'let me think about it.' Your gut read is:

options.text: That's a polite no, so you push once more before hanging up
That's genuine, so you ask what would help them decide and agree a real follow-up
That's a stall, so you offer a discount on the ask to close it now
That's fine, you thank them and end the call with no follow-up planned
You ask directly whether it's really a no

questions.prompt: The donor's answers turn one-word partway through what had been an easy chat. You:

options.text: Assume it's nothing and keep going as planned
Speed up to get to the ask before they lose interest completely
Ask directly if they need to go
Name the change and hand them the option to stop or continue
Lower your energy to match theirs and see what happens

questions.prompt: You name the monthly amount and the donor gives a short, nervous laugh. You:

options.text: Laugh along and immediately suggest a smaller number
Ignore it and wait for their answer
Name it lightly: 'that got a laugh, was it more than you expected?'
Explain the reasoning behind the suggested amount
Ask if a different amount would suit them better

questions.prompt: EQ Identity EQ1

options.text: When a donor gets emotional, my strength is staying calm and not reacting
My strength is using their emotion as information to guide what I say next
My strength is noticing the emotion before they've said anything
My strength is naming the emotion out loud, even when it's uncomfortable

questions.prompt: EQ Identity EQ2

options.text: Under pressure on a call, I stay logical and don't let the knock-backs get to me
Under pressure on a call, I look for the emotional opening the donor hasn't noticed yet
Under pressure on a call, I watch and wait, reading their tone before I act
Under pressure on a call, I call out what's really happening, even if it's awkward

questions.prompt: EQ Identity EQ3

options.text: After a tough call, I debrief by reviewing what I said and whether it was accurate
After a tough call, I think about what emotional opening I did or didn't use
After a tough call, I replay what I noticed: tone, pauses, energy
After a tough call, I think about whether I named the hard thing or talked around it
